data.title: Urgent payment demand with changed bank details – likely phishing
data.summary: A letter purporting to be from Stadtwerke Musterstadt's customer service asks for an urgent €214.00 advance payment (Abschlag) to a newly announced bank account by 11 September 2026, threatening to cut off the electricity supply without further notice if unpaid. Several details in the letter strongly suggest this is a phishing/fraud attempt rather than a genuine communication from the utility.
data.explanation: This letter claims to be from your electricity provider and asks you to send €214.00 to a new bank account within a few days, threatening to cut your power if you don't pay. Several signs suggest this may be a phishing scam: the new account is held by a company with a foreign legal form (s.r.o.), the IBAN given fails the standard IBAN checksum check, the letter asks you not to reply through normal channels and to call only one specific number, and the sender's email address uses a placeholder-style domain. Do not transfer any money to the account shown in this letter. Instead, contact Stadtwerke Musterstadt directly using contact details from a previous, trusted bill or their official website to verify whether this letter is genuine before taking any action.

items.action: Do not pay to the IBAN given in this letter. First verify with Stadtwerke Musterstadt directly, using contact details from a previous trusted bill or their official website, whether this letter and the new bank account are genuine.
items.consequence: The letter claims the electricity supply will be disconnected without further notice if the payment is not received by the stated deadline.
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den fälligen Abschlag von 214,00 € bis spätestens 11.09.2026.

warnings: This letter shows multiple strong signs of being a phishing scam impersonating a utility company: a sudden, urgent change of bank details to an account held by a company with a foreign legal form (s.r.o.) is a classic fraud pattern.
The IBAN printed in the letter (DE61 2004 1111 0512 3456 78) fails the standard IBAN checksum validation, suggesting it may be fabricated.
The letter asks the recipient not to reply through normal channels and to call only one specific phone number, which is a common tactic to prevent verification of a scam.
The sender's email address uses the domain 'kundenservice-mail.example', which is not a genuine, verifiable company domain.

Do not transfer money to the account in this letter; verify directly with Stadtwerke Musterstadt using contact details from a previous, trusted bill or their official website before taking any action.
